name: Jinja Town Centre
tagline: The colonial grid, with the verandas and the market
description: The town's centre laid out on a grid by the British and built up by the Indian trading community, with deep-veranda shophouses along Main Street that survive largely intact. The market, the banks and the bus stage are here. It is compact, walkable and the practical heart of Jinja.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the market, the shops and the transport on foot
pros: Everything practical within a ten-minute walk
cons: Dusty and noisy in the dry season

name: The Source of the Nile
tagline: Where the river leaves Lake Victoria
description: The riverside area at the point where the Nile flows out of Lake Victoria, marked by gardens on both banks and a small monument to Speke. Boats run out to the spring in the middle of the channel. It is quiet, green and a short ride from the centre, with a handful of lodges along the bank.
bestFor: Stays wanting the river at the door and the town a short ride away
pros: The Nile and the lake outlet on the doorstep
Green, quiet and cooler than the centre
Boat trips and birdlife directly accessible
cons: Ten minutes from the town's services
Entry fees apply at the main viewing gardens
Mosquitoes near the water at dusk

name: Bujagali and the Rapids
tagline: Upriver where the rafting starts, among the lodges
description: The stretch of river north of town where the white water begins and where the rafting companies, campsites and backpacker lodges have concentrated for two decades. The Bujagali dam changed some of the rapids, which remains a live local grievance, but the remaining runs are still substantial.
bestFor: Anyone here for the rafting and kayaking, with the town accepted as a ride
pros: Rafting and kayaking operators on the doorstep
Riverside lodges and a genuine traveller community
cons: Twenty minutes from Jinja by boda boda
Seasonal, quieter outside the main months

name: Walukuba and the Eastern Suburbs
tagline: Residential Jinja, where the town actually lives
description: The residential districts east and south of the centre, built partly as housing for the old industrial works, with ordinary Ugandan family homes, local markets and schools. Rents here are the lowest in Jinja and it is a genuinely local neighbourhood with no tourist presence at all.
bestFor: Long stays wanting local prices and a real neighbourhood
pros: The lowest rents in the town
Local markets and food at genuine prices
A settled community rather than a transient one

name: Mabira Forest (30 km west)
description: A substantial rainforest reserve on the road towards Kampala, with a canopy walkway, primates including red-tailed monkeys and grey-cheeked mangabeys, and a network of trails. A couple of eco-lodges operate inside it. It is genuinely quiet and green, and the road runs straight through the middle.
bestFor: Short stays in the forest rather than a base
pros: On the main road between Jinja and Kampala
cons: Thirty minutes from Jinja and no services nearby
Accommodation is lodges rather than rentals
